title: Set 57

sentences.ko: 샤워기 헤드 고치는 법을 좀 찾아보려고 앉았는데, 그건 4분쯤 걸렸고, 어쩌다 보니 사람들이 녹슨 옛날 공구 복원하는 걸 보고 있더라고. 그다음엔 누가 30분 동안 프라이팬 닦는 걸 보고 있었고. 차는 다 식었고 샤워기 헤드는 아직도 고장 난 채야.
sentences.text: I sat down to look up how to fix the shower head, and that took me about four minutes, and then somehow I'm watching guys restore old rusty tools, and then somebody cleaning a pan for half an hour. My tea went cold and the shower head is still broken.

alts.text: So I'm googling how to fix the shower head, right, and that's maybe four minutes, and next thing I know I'm watching dudes restore rusty old tools, then some guy cleaning a pan for half an hour. Tea's stone cold and the shower head's still busted.

I sat down to research how to repair the shower head, which took approximately four minutes, and then somehow I found myself watching men restore old rusty tools, followed by someone cleaning a pan for half an hour. My tea went cold and the shower head remains broken.

sentences.note: **look up** 은 궁금한 것을 찾아본다는 뜻입니다. **somehow** 는 나도 모르게 어쩌다 보니 그렇게 됐다고 할 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: 유튜브 보다가 시간 다 날린 얘기

sentences.ko: 에스프레소 머신을 하나 샀는데, 커피가 맛있는 건 인정해. 그런데 매번 씻어야 할 부품이 여섯 개쯤 돼서, 출근하는 아침에는 그냥 안 하고 어차피 길모퉁이 카페에 들러. 그래서 지금 커피값을 두 번 내고 있고, 그 기계는 조리대를 절반이나 차지하고 있어.
sentences.text: I got this espresso machine, and it makes good coffee, I'll give it that, but there's like six parts to wash every time, so on a work morning I don't bother and I stop at the place on the corner anyway. So now I'm paying for coffee twice and that thing is taking up half my counter.

alts.text: So I bought this espresso machine, and yeah, the coffee's good, I'll give it that, but there's like six parts to wash every single time, so on a work morning I can't be bothered and I stop at the place on the corner anyway. So now I'm paying for coffee twice and that thing's eating up half my counter.

I purchased an espresso machine, and it does make good coffee, I will grant it that, but there are about six parts to wash every time, so on a work morning I do not bother and I stop at the shop on the corner regardless. So I am now paying for coffee twice, and the machine occupies half of my counter.

sentences.note: **I'll give it that** 은 다른 건 몰라도 그 점 하나는 인정한다고 할 때 쓰는 말입니다. **taking up** 은 자리를 차지한다는 뜻입니다.

sentences.ko: 일요일에 처남이랑 농구를 했어. 30분쯤 했나. 그날 밤에는 아주 멀쩡했거든. 그런데 이틀 뒤인 화요일에 확 오더라고. 지금은 옆구리가 너무 아파서 재채기하기가 무서워.
sentences.text: Me and my brother in law played basketball Sunday, maybe half an hour, and I felt totally fine that night. Then it hit me Tuesday, two days later, and now my sides hurt so bad I'm scared to sneeze.

alts.text: Played basketball with my brother in law Sunday, half an hour tops, and I was totally fine that night. Then it hits me Tuesday and now my sides hurt so bad I'm scared to sneeze.

My brother in law and I played basketball on Sunday, perhaps half an hour, and I felt entirely fine that evening. It caught up with me on Tuesday, two days later, and now my sides ache so badly that I am afraid to sneeze.

sentences.note: **it hit me** 는 아픈 게 뒤늦게 확 왔다고 할 때 씁니다. **so bad** 는 아주 심하게라는 뜻으로, 회화에서 badly 대신 흔히 이렇게 말합니다.

sentences.ko: 우리 팀에 나한테 메일 보낼 때마다 팀장을 참조로 넣는 여자가 있어. 그냥 그 파일 좀 보내 줄래 하는 메일에도 그래. 그러니까 그 사람이 하루 종일 나를 쫓아다니면서 재촉하는 것처럼 보이는데, 나는 아무 말도 못 해. 내가 뭘 어쩌겠어, 우리 팀장 참조에 그만 넣으라고 말해? 그게 어떻게 들리는지 너도 알잖아.
sentences.text: There's a woman on my team who copies my manager on every email she sends me, even when it's just, hey, can you send me that file. So it looks like she's chasing me down all day, and I can't say anything, because what am I going to do, ask her to stop copying my boss? You hear how that sounds.

alts.text: I've got someone on my team who copies my manager on every email she sends me, even when it's just, hey, send me that file. So it looks like she's chasing me down all day, and I can't say anything, cause what am I gonna do, ask her to quit copying my boss? You hear how that sounds.

There is a woman on my team who copies my manager on every email she sends me, even when it is simply a request for a file. It gives the impression that she is pursuing me all day, and I cannot say anything, because what am I to do, ask her to stop copying my supervisor? You can hear how that sounds.

sentences.note: **copies my manager on every email** 처럼 copy A on B 는 메일 참조에 넣는다는 뜻입니다. **chasing me down** 은 답을 받아 내려고 계속 쫓아다니며 재촉한다는 말입니다.
sentences.situation: 회사 사람 때문에 짜증난 걸 친구한테 털어놓기

sentences.ko: 우유랑 빵이랑 저녁거리나 사려고 잠깐 들렀는데, 62달러가 나왔어. 뭔가 잘못된 게 틀림없다는 듯이 계산 화면만 멍하니 쳐다보고 서 있었어. 그 봉투에 비싼 건 하나도 없었다니까! 그래, 나도 내가 매번 이 소리 하는 거 알아. 근데 매번 오르니까 그렇지.
sentences.text: I ran in for milk and bread and something for dinner, and it came to sixty two dollars, and I just stood there staring at the screen like it had to be a mistake. There was nothing fancy in that bag! And yeah, I know I say this every time, but that's because it goes up every time.

alts.text: Popped in for milk and bread and something for dinner, and it came out to sixty two dollars, and I'm just standing there staring at the screen like it's gotta be a mistake. There was nothing fancy in that bag! And yeah, I know I say this every time, but that's cause it goes up every time.

I stopped in for milk, bread, and something for dinner, and the total came to sixty two dollars, and I simply stood there staring at the screen as though it had to be a mistake. There was nothing extravagant in that bag. And yes, I am aware that I say this every time, but that is because it increases every time.

sentences.note: **ran in for** 는 뭘 사러 가게에 잠깐 들어갔다 나온다는 뜻입니다. **came to** 는 값이 얼마 나왔다고 할 때 쓰는 말입니다.

reviewed: 3번 casual: 뒷부분이 text 와 거의 글자까지 똑같아서 말투를 바꾼 것이 아니었습니다. 더 짧고 구어답게 다시 썼습니다 (half an hour tops, I was totally fine, 뒷마디 정리).
2번 formal: there are some six parts 는 어색합니다. some 을 이런 자리에 쓰면 옛날 글투로 들려서 about 으로 바꿨습니다.
2번 casual: eating half my counter 는 원어민이 이렇게 끊어 말하지 않습니다. eating up half my counter 로 고쳤습니다.
